tasks.title: Add review_converge_on workflow field + validation
tasks.acceptance: review_converge_on workflow field exists with values blocking|all, built-in default blocking. It resolves through the layer order (CLI > env > task override > project config > built-in) and appears in tp config --resolved. It is settable via tp set --workflow review_converge_on=<value> and tp set --workflow --project review_converge_on=<value> (writes .tp/config.json). tasks.title: Severity-aware clean predicate (blocking vs all)
tasks.acceptance: A counted review round is clean per review_converge_on: under blocking, clean when no surviving finding is critical or high severity (severity matched case-insensitively); under all, clean when zero findings of any severity survive. The clean decision reads the surviving set (recorded findings minus those resolved wontfix/duplicate) live from the round record, so switching review_converge_on or resolving a finding wontfix re-evaluates a round in --status without re-recording. A surviving finding whose severity is missing or outside critical|high|medium|low is treated as blocking (per-finding, uniform every round); a round none of whose surviving findings carry a severity is clean iff zero survive. Audit convergence stays status-based and is unaffected. When a consuming command (tp review --status/--record) resolves an invalid winning review_converge_on value from a stored layer (env, .tp/config.json, or task override), it exits 1 (validation) with the legal-values hint.
source_sections: ## 4. The blocking-severity set and recorded justification
tasks.closed_reason:
- Under review_converge_on=blocking a round is clean iff no surviving finding is critical or high severity (case-insensitive); engine.ReviewRoundClean in reviewclean.go, covered by reviewclean_test.go.
- Under review_converge_on=all a round is clean iff zero findings of any severity survive; covered by reviewclean_test.go.
- Clean is recomputed LIVE from the surviving set (recorded findings minus wontfix/duplicate-with-evidence) by re-reading the round findings file, so switching review_converge_on and resolving a blocking finding wontfix after record both re-evaluate in tp review --status without re-recording; covered by reviewconvergeon_clean_test.go.
- A surviving finding whose severity is missing or outside critical|high|medium|low is treated as blocking (per-finding, uniform every round); covered by reviewclean_test.go.
- A round none of whose surviving findings carry a valid severity is clean iff zero survive; covered by reviewclean_test.go and pre-release back-compat.
- Audit convergence stays status-based and is unaffected; tp audit ignores review_converge_on; covered by reviewconvergeon_clean_test.go.
- A consuming command (tp review --status/--record) resolving an invalid winning review_converge_on from a stored layer exits 1 (validation) with the legal-values hint; covered by reviewconvergeon_clean_test.go. Gate: go test ./... ok, golangci-lint 0 issues; budget/import/prompt-gen frozen-flag divergence tracked as unify-convergence-consumers.

tasks.title: Recorded harness note (--harness-note, harness_stale)
tasks.acceptance: tp review <spec> --record <file> --harness-note "<text>" and the tp audit equivalent store the note verbatim on the recorded round; omitting the flag records nothing. --status reports harness_stale and, when true, harness_note. harness_stale is true only when the two most recent recorded rounds both carry non-empty notes differing after trimming surrounding whitespace; false when either note is empty (predate or opt-out) or fewer than two rounds recorded; comparison is per phase (review vs audit rounds separately). harness_note is emitted only when harness_stale is true, otherwise omitted (never "" or null), and when emitted is the verbatim stored note. Supplying --harness-note without --record is a usage error (exit 2).
tasks.closed_reason:
- tp review <spec> --record <file> --harness-note stores the note verbatim on the review round and the tp audit equivalent on the audit round; HarnessNote omitempty field on the shared ReviewRound, covered by harness_note_test.go.
- Omitting the --harness-note flag stores nothing and behaves exactly as before; covered by the omit-stores-nothing test.
- tp review --status and tp audit --status report harness_stale and, when true, harness_note (read-only, alongside roles_stale); covered by harness_note_test.go.
- harness_stale is true only when the two most recent rounds both carry non-empty notes that differ after trimming surrounding whitespace; engine.HarnessStale, covered by harness_stale_test.go.
- harness_stale is false when either note is empty (predate or opt-out), whitespace-only, or fewer than two rounds are recorded; covered by harness_stale_test.go.
- The two-round comparison is per phase (review --status compares review rounds only, audit --status audit rounds only); covered by the interleaved-phase isolation test.
- harness_note is emitted only when harness_stale is true, otherwise omitted (never '' or null), and when emitted is the verbatim stored note; LatestHarnessNote + omission/verbatim assertions. --record computes staleness after storing the current round's note.
- Supplying --harness-note without --record is a usage error (exit 2) with a requires---record hint, on both review and audit; covered by harness_note_test.go. Gate: go test ./... ok, golangci-lint 0 issues.

tasks.title: next_action for review and audit loops
tasks.acceptance: tp review --status/--record and the audit equivalents carry a next_action naming the single next step by a fixed precedence total over reachable states: converged names the phase forward step; convergence-blocking unresolved findings name the revise-and-re-review directive (never --resolve/--resolve-all/--verify); a mechanizable mechanize_candidates class present and none blocking names register-a-check-then-run-the-next-round (over-specification is un-mechanizable and does not trigger this branch, falling through); a clean-but-not-yet-converged round names the next-round command. It gates no exit code. tp resolves <spec>/<base> in emitted command strings; <file> and the checks template stay literal.
